result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 2 FOUND, 3 NOT_FOUND; the two FOUND rules describe one underlying JWT signing-key vulnerability
evidence: Read-only review of authorization constants, identity seeding, token signing, bearer-token verification, administrator endpoint authorization, and authentication paths.
Confirmed that a source-embedded key is actively used for JWT signing and validation without a development-only guard.
Seeded demonstration account passwords were observed but excluded as sample credentials; no literal password or signing-key value is disclosed.

Limitations: no live forged-token submission, deployed-secret inventory, filesystem/cloud permission inspection, or operational logging audit. NOT_FOUND for hard-coded passwords reflects the sample-credential exclusion, not absence of password defaults. Tests, generated code, setup/context files, generated reports, and .github/agents were excluded. NOT_FOUND indicates no confirmed reportable exploit, not proof of absence.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: HIGH impact; confidence 9/10. AuthorizationConstants embeds the JWT signing key as a source constant. IdentityTokenClaimService.GetTokenAsync uses it for HMAC-SHA256 signing at lines 26 and 41. PublicApi startup uses the same constant as its bearer-token verification key at lines 54-69, without a development-only guard or configurable replacement. An attacker who knows the source can sign a JWT containing the administrator role and a future expiration, then access administrator catalog mutation endpoints. The key is an active trust anchor, not merely unused example data. Its literal value is intentionally omitted. Verified through static signing, validation, and authorization data flow; no live forged token was submitted.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: HIGH impact; confidence 9/10. The hard-coded JWT signing credential is also an instance of CWE-798. IdentityTokenClaimService signs with the source constant and PublicApi validates bearer tokens with it. Source knowledge therefore permits forging an administrator token without authenticating. This is the same underlying vulnerability as CWE-321, recorded separately because the checklist requires one result for each rule; deduplicate it when counting unique vulnerabilities. Literal signing-key and sample-password values are intentionally omitted.
